claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi powder is treated as a high-entropy-alloy feedstock.
A specifically designed feedstock with optimized chemistry and processing conditions can overcome the limitations of conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed intervention can reduce the processing complexity of metallic additive manufacturing.
The intervention is applicable to L-PBF or SLM processing of AlCrFeNiSi.
Optimizing feedstock chemistry and processing conditions will produce an optimized grain size and grain distribution.
The optimized feedstock will promote a more uniform microstructure.
Joint optimization of alloy composition and processing conditions can reduce lack-of-fusion, balling, and keyholing defects.
A more uniform microstructure and fewer process defects will reduce residual thermal stresses.
A more uniform microstructure and fewer process defects will improve mechanical properties.
The optimized feedstock will increase additive-manufacturing processing reliability.
The predicted improvements apply to additively manufactured miniature components.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing produces higher residual stress, poorer mechanical properties, and lower reliability than the proposed optimized-feedstock route.
The exact optimal AlCrFeNiSi composition and processing conditions are currently unknown.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as using an already optimized composition and process, while the uncertainty field states that the optimal composition and processing conditions are unknown.
The proposal calls this a single intervention, but it combines feedstock-composition redesign with optimization of processing conditions, which are distinct intervention dimensions.
